title: Agreement of two definitions of the uniform expectation
statement:
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function of arity $n$. Then the two forms of the uniform expectation of $f$ coincide, namely
\[
  \frac{1}{2^n} \sum_{x \in \{0,1\}^n} f(x) \;=\; 2^{-n} \sum_{x \in \{0,1\}^n} f(x).
\]
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean function of arity n (f : {0,1}^n → ℝ)
replaced:
The locally-defined expectation \texttt{BoolFourier.expectation} agrees with
\texttt{BooleanAnalysis.expect}: for every $f$, $\mathbb{E}[f] = \mathrm{expect}(f)$.
